title: Injury, bleeding or burn
summary: Reported blow, injury, bleeding or burn. Separate the mechanism, the level of consciousness and whether the bleeding continues. Contusion or concussion are hypotheses that require evidence of the event and relevant symptoms. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. No clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

heavy_bleeding.text: Heavy bleeding that continues: emergency. Press on the wound now.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Press directly on the wound with a sterile dressing, a clean cloth or clothing (or your hand) and keep pressing until it stops.
If blood soaks through the dressing, do not remove it: put another one on top and keep pressing.
Do not remove objects stuck in the wound.
Lie down and raise your feet about 30 cm if there is no head, neck, back or leg injury.
Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it gets better.

notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Move away from whatever is burning or giving off smoke.
Cover the burn with a dry sterile dressing or a clean cloth and raise it above the heart if you can.
Do not apply ointments, ice or cold water to a severe burn, do not break blisters and do not remove clothing stuck to the skin.
Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Another crew member: check that the person is breathing; start CPR if needed. If it could be electrical, do not touch the person directly.

head_injury_red_flags.text: Blow to the head with danger signs: emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Another crew member: stay with the person and monitor their level of consciousness.

review.text: Injury without warning signs: tend to it and monitor. If the bleeding does not stop or, after a blow to the head, repeated vomiting or worsening confusion appears, it is an emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Superficial wound: wash it with soap and water, dry it and press with a clean cloth if it bleeds.
Minor burn with intact skin: cool it with cool (not ice-cold) water for 5 to 30 minutes and cover it with a dry dressing.
After a blow to the head, monitor for hours: repeated vomiting, increasing confusion, drowsiness, slurred speech or a worsening headache are an emergency.

candidates.label: Contusion
candidates.minimum_evidence: Reported blow with localized pain, swelling or bruising.

candidates.label: Concussion
candidates.minimum_evidence: Blow to the head with headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting or confusion.

sources.title: CDC HEADS UP: Signs and Symptoms
